What graph would be appropriate in these situations?

1. The health of the Brisbane River is a concern to many residents and scientists.
   An Australian study [@data:Goonetilleke2009:PortOfBrisbane] compared nine different and diverse sites in the Brisbane River near the Port of Brisbane.
      
   At each site, they obtain numerous measurements of the total nitrogen concentration (in mg/L).  
      
   The researchers wished to study the relationship between the sites and the nitrogen concentration measurements.

2. In studies of childhood obesity, studies have found that children who eat breakfast cereal were leaner 
   than those who do not eat breakfast cereal.
   A study [@data:Frantzen2013:Cereal] examined a large number of children from low-income families to explore the effect of ready-to-eat breakfast cereals in these children.  
      
   For each child, the researchers recorded the body mass index (BMI) percentile for each child, and the number of days that each child ate ready-to-eat-breakfast-cereal. (RTEC; the numbers of days out of the nine days studied.)
      
   The researchers wished to examine the relationship between the BMI and RTEC for the children.
